questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Fiji?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Fiji article.

questions.proof: The capital city and the city with the most people is Suva.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Fiji?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Fiji article.

questions.proof: The official languages of Fiji are Fijian, English and Hindi Fiji is part of the Pacific Rim.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Fiji was a British colony up until _____; British occupation lasted almost a century.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Fiji article.

questions.proof: Fiji was a British colony up until 1970; British occupation lasted almost a century.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Most visitors are from _____, New Zealand and the USA.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Zealand”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Fiji article, under the heading “Tourism”.

questions.proof: Most visitors are from Australia, New Zealand and the USA.
